issue_context.title: BUG: pandas.read_sql_query type hint only allows str params
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the main branch of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas
import sqlalchemy.engine


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sql_connection: str = "driver={ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server};server=myServer;database=myDatabase;trusted_connection=yes"
    sql_engine: sqlalchemy.engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine(
        url=sqlalchemy.engine.URL.create(drivername="mssql+pyodbc", query={"odbc_connect": sql_connection})
    )
    with sql_engine.connect() as connection:
        myarg1: int = 10
        myarg2: bool = True
        result: pandas.DataFrame = pandas.read_sql_query(
            sql="""
                DECLARE @arg1 INT = ?;
                DECLARE @arg2 INT = ?
                
                SELECT
                    arg1 = @arg1,
                    arg2 = @arg2
            """,
            con=connection,
            params=[myarg1, myarg2]
        )
        print(result)
```
```


### Issue Description

Pandas 1.4.4 allowed pandas.read_sql_query to be called with params that included int, bool, datetime.date, etc. Pandas 1.5.1 only allows params  that are str. Code that attempts to pass int or bool to a SQL script that is expecting INT parameters fails code inspection. For example, Code Inspection in PyCharm reports the following for the call to pandas.read_sql_query:

Unexpected type(s): (str, Any, list[Union[int, bool]]) Possible type(s): (Any, Any, Union(list[str], dict[str, str], None]) (Any, Any, Union(list[str], dict[str, str], None])

This new behavior is a regression,

### Expected Behavior

The  type hint for params should be defined as typing.Optional[typing.Union[typing.List, typing.Mapping]] so that list of any objects or any dicts can be passed as was t he case with Pandas 1.4.4.

Hi, this is my first time participating in the `pandas` project. Not sure if this is the correct place to post results of my own investigation/triage. Please advise if I should take it elsewhere, Thank you.

Comparing the source code between `main` and tag `v1.4.4` it seems like there are additional type hints added to the `read_sql_query` function:

```python
# v1.4.4
def read_sql_query(
    sql,
    con,
    index_col=None,
    coerce_float: bool = True,
    params=None,
    parse_dates=None,
    chunksize: int | None = None,
    dtype: DtypeArg | None = None,
) -> DataFrame | Iterator[DataFrame]:
...

# v1.5.0 and newer
def read_sql_query(
    sql,
    con,
    index_col: str | list[str] | None = None,
    coerce_float: bool = True,
    params: list[str] | dict[str, str] | None = None,
    parse_dates: list[str] | dict[str, str] | None = None,
    chunksize: int | None = None,
    dtype: DtypeArg | None = None,
) -> DataFrame | Iterator[DataFrame]:
...
```

On the other hand, at `main`, a similar function `read_sql` does not have type hints for the `params` argument

```python
def read_sql(
    sql,
    con,
    index_col: str | list[str] | None = None,
    coerce_float: bool = True,
    params=None,
    parse_dates=None,
    columns: list[str] | None = None,
    chunksize: int | None = None,
) -> DataFrame | Iterator[DataFrame]:
```

From v1.4.4 to v1.5.0 it seem that:
1. Additional hints were applied to the `params` argument in `read_sql_query`
2. Such hints were not applied to other methods with similar signatures and arguments

Based on that, removing the type hints on `params` seems to be a straightforward fix, unless there is value to be gained from the additional type hints that I am not aware of (in which case please advise).

On the other hand, I noticed that the `parse_dates` argument in `read_sql_query` also had additional type hints newly applied in v1.5.0 (but not applied in `read_sql`). Without digging further, I am not sure if there are other examples of misplaced type hints and their impacts.

Upon a second look it seems like the type hint for `parse_dates` was also inaccurate:

```python
def read_sql_query(
    sql,
    con,
    index_col: str | list[str] | None = None,
    coerce_float: bool = True,
    params= None,
    parse_dates: list[str] | dict[str, str] | None = None,
    chunksize: int | None = None,
    dtype: DtypeArg | None = None,
) -> DataFrame | Iterator[DataFrame]:
    """
    ...
    parse_dates : list or dict, default: None
        - List of column names to parse as dates.
        - Dict of ``{column_name: format string}`` where format string is
          strftime compatible in case of parsing string times, or is one of
          (D, s, ns, ms, us) in case of parsing integer timestamps.
        - Dict of ``{column_name: arg dict}``, where the arg dict corresponds
          to the keyword arguments of :func:`pandas.to_datetime`
          Especially useful with databases without native Datetime support,
          such as SQLite.
    ...
    """
...
```

Based on the docstring, `parse_dates` should accept `dict[str, dict]` in addition to `list[str] | dict[str, str]` for passing keyword arguments of the function `pandas.to_datetime`.
Thank you for your prompt response.

I have tried pandas 2.0.3 but read_sql_query still throws code inspection
errors in PyCharm when passing a parameter dict[str, bool] or dict[are,
datetime.date]. I thought tiyr fix would allow one to pass dict[str, Any].

I am using mssql+pyodbc with SqlAlchemy. Your suggestion to use an adapter
doesn't work with mssql package since that package does not expose a
register_adapter method.

Thanks,
Jayanth

review_comments: Can the Any been made more specific?

I think this is one of the rare cases where `Any` is correct. See the type hint in SQLAlchemy which we are calling into here:
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/e79ab08165e01dc7af50fcffadb31468ace51b6c/lib/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py#L1370-L1376
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/e79ab08165e01dc7af50fcffadb31468ace51b6c/lib/sqlalchemy/engine/interfaces.py#L224-L229
